subject: history
topicName: Nazi Racial Policy and the Holocaust

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Nazis believed in a racial hierarchy with the "Aryan" race (tall, blonde, blue-eyed Germans and Nordics) at the top as the "master race" (Herrenvolk). At the bottom were "sub-humans" (Untermenschen) - Jews, Roma, Slavs, and black people. Hitler wrote in Mein Kampf (1925): "The Jew is and remains the eternal enemy of the Aryan."

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Persecution of Jews began immediately after Hitler became Chancellor. On 1 April 1933, the Nazis organised a nationwide boycott of Jewish shops and businesses. SA men stood outside Jewish shops with signs reading "Germans! Defend yourselves! Don't buy from Jews!"

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: At the Nuremberg Rally on 15 September 1935, Hitler announced two laws that fundamentally changed the legal status of German Jews: the Reich Citizenship Law and the Law for the Protection of German Blood and Honour. These laws stripped Jews of citizenship and banned marriages between Jews and Germans.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Nuremberg Laws were a turning point because they made anti-Semitism legal and official. Before 1935, persecution had been through SA violence and local regulations; after 1935, it was enshrined in national law. This gave persecution the authority of the state and made it systematic.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain how the Nuremberg Laws affected the lives of German Jews. (4 marks) | Why was Kristallnacht a significant turning point? (8 marks) | "The persecution of the Jews escalated gradually between 1933 and 1945." How far do you agree? (12 marks)

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always trace the ESCALATION: boycott → laws → violence → ghettos → genocide. Examiners want to see you understand the progression Use specific dates: Nuremberg Laws 15 September 1935, Kristallnacht 9-10 November 1938, Wannsee 20 January 1942 The death toll is approximately 6 million Jews - always include this figure Kristallnacht was organised by Goebbels, not "spontaneous" - the SA and SS were in civilian clothes to maintain the pretence For resistance questions, acknowledge the extreme difficulty but give specific examples of those who tried The Wannsee Conference was about LOGISTICS, not decision-making - the genocide had already begun Remember that other groups were also persecuted: Roma, disabled, Slavs, homosexuals
